                 G6 LANDOWNERS LEGAL FUND, LLC’S REPLY BRIEF

       COMES NOW, G6 Landowners Legal Fund, LLC (“G6 Landowners”), and files this its

Reply Brief to address issues and arguments raised by other parties in this matter regarding the

factors needed by the Administrative Law Judges (“ALJs”) and the Public Utility Commission of

Texas (the “Commission”) in identifying the route that best meets the statutory and regulatory

requirements applicable to this proceeding. The Initial Briefs confirm that Route 894, as proposed

by the Applicants, best complies with the statutory and regulatory factors that govern this

proceeding and should be recommended by the ALJs and adopted by the Commission.

       This Reply Brief includes two parts. First, the Brief validates the comprehensive process

used by the Applicants to identify Route 894 as the “best meets” route in this proceeding. Second,

the Brief summarizes the bases for selecting Route 894 over routes proposed by other Intervenors

and responds to specific issues raised by those Intervenors in their respective Initial Briefs.


                                                    1
            G6 Landowners and several other parties have recognized that there is no perfect route for

the proposed Project. No party wants the route to affect its property. It has been appropriately

noted, however, “A landowner not wanting the line on or near their property is not a differentiating

factor in selecting a route for the line.” 1 The selection of any of the proposed routes will take a toll

on the communities affected. These facts mandate a thorough review of all the factors.

           G6 Landowners appreciates the difficult position in which this proceeding puts the ALJs

and the Commission. While the scope of this proceeding is immense and the consequences are

considerable, there is a straight-forward resolution supported by the significant record established

first through the Applicants routing study which found Route 894 to be the “best meets” route and

supplemented by multiple parties each bringing their own perspective and experience to the

analysis. Based on this record, the ALJs should propose and the Commission should adopt Route

894 as the “best meets” route in this proceeding.

           I.       The Record Confirms Selection of Route 894 as the “Best Meets” Route

                     A.       The Applicants’ Analysis

           The Applicants have stated repeatedly that they will accept the Commission’s decision to

adopt any of the proposed routes.2 The Applicants are one of two parties in this proceeding (the

other being Commission staff) that have no bias or self-interest favoring the selection of one route

over another. But the Applicants did have a regulatory obligation to perform an in-depth analysis

of the potential routes for its project in advance of filing the Application. Section 17 of the

Application requires completion of a Routing Study and requires that the Applicants “State which

route the applicant believes best addresses the requirements of PURA and P.U.C. Substantive

Rules.”
